requirements.title: Dated list and restricted approved additions
requirements.summary: The publicly linked requirements document is updated September 27, 2024. Later approved nominations are kept on a Stanford-login spreadsheet, which was not accessed. The public list cannot establish the full current approved pool.

requirements.title: Unit minimum and host-core overlap
requirements.summary: Each course must carry at least three units; this is a minimum, not verified exact course credit. If the earlier concentration requirements overlap the core, add approved contingent electives to reach five courses beyond the core.

requirements.title: Recommended preparation
requirements.summary: CS 161 before CS 221 is recommended, not stated here as an unconditional prerequisite.

requirements.title: Concentration versus core grades
requirements.summary: Concentration courses require D− or better, while core courses require C− or better. A compulsory no-option pass/S equivalent can qualify; optional credit/no-credit cannot. When a course also serves a core role, do not infer that the lower concentration threshold overrides the core rule.

requirements.title: Five courses, units and cross-list equivalence
requirements.summary: The concentration comprises five courses, normally at least three units each. An approved cross-list registration can meet the same requirement unless explicitly excluded; aliases are not additional compulsory courses.

requirements.title: Internal overlap and contingent electives
requirements.summary: Ordinarily a course fills one required course in core or concentration. The seminar/integrative asterisk exceptions permit specified cross-application; if a core-counted course satisfies a concentration area, an approved contingent elective preserves five concentration courses beyond the core.

requirements.title: Other major, minor and coterminal overlap
requirements.summary: A secondary major differs from a double/multiple major: the former permits broad overlap, while the latter normally requires separate courses except shared introductory skills. Minor overlap is generally restricted by the minor program. Units cannot count toward both undergraduate and graduate careers; an approved replacement may be needed.

requirements.title: Version and graduation course plan
requirements.summary: Use requirements active when the declaration is approved or a complete later version, not an arbitrary blend. Submit the final course plan at least two quarters before graduation, verify future offerings and secure approval of unlisted replacements.

requirements.title: Host-major declaration
requirements.summary: To declare the host Symbolic Systems major, complete at least one Stanford quarter and take SYMSYS 1 or remain enrolled beyond its drop deadline; file Axess declaration and a course plan, attend an advising-fellow interview and receive the Student Services Officer’s approval. Junior declarations also require a confirmed concentration advisor.

requirements.title: Concentration advisor eligibility and deadline
requirements.summary: Select a concentration advisor by junior autumn; juniors declaring the major need one already confirmed. The advisor must hold an ongoing Stanford instructional appointment, not a visiting/short-term role, and have relevant expertise; SymSys affiliation is unnecessary.

requirements.title: Advisor confirmation and capstone changes
requirements.summary: Confirm the willing advisor through the program office with the advisor copied. Lack of an advisor can hold junior-winter registration. The advisor must approve the capstone and later revisions before the final graduation plan.

requirements.title: Individual replacement petitions
requirements.summary: An individual replacement petition must fit a published category and be approved; submit before the relevant quarter where course planning depends on it. Same-area/level and minimum-unit/grade rules remain applicable. Approved combinations require all component courses; they are not interchangeable alternatives.

requirements.title: External equivalence versus program elective
requirements.summary: An external course with approved Stanford course equivalence can qualify without further SymSys approval if it meets major policies. Otherwise a program-elective replacement petition needs evidence of comparable content, rigor, prerequisites and units, plus official transcript and registrar certification; approval is conditional until all steps finish.

requirements.title: Online mathematics date restriction
requirements.summary: Online external mathematics courses are ineligible for SymSys transfer consideration from July 1, 2026; the explicitly documented earlier accommodation is not a current blanket permission.

requirements.title: Other replacement categories
requirements.summary: The public policy also governs certified individual equivalence, version transitions, discontinued courses and grade replacements. A grade-replacement approval requires the original unqualified course on the final transcript; a replacement alone does not erase that condition. Graduate-only core waivers are outside this undergraduate concentration scope.

requirements.title: Transfer credit grade, units and duplicates
requirements.summary: External work needs accredited college-level eligibility and C− or better; a pass must be documented equivalent. The university caps combined external/test credit at 45 quarter units, or 90 for transfer entrants. The registrar converts/rounds units under its published formula; later duplicate Stanford enrollment removes the matching transfer credit. These are university limits, not invented concentration-specific caps.

requirements.title: Transfer evaluation deadlines
requirements.summary: Course-to-course requests for prematriculation work belong in the first three quarters; postmatriculation requests generally have a one-year window. Final approval requires a directly submitted official transcript. Department discretion governs program-elective timing, and graduating students must meet the registrar’s final-quarter deadlines.

requirements.title: Nomination decisions remain access-restricted
requirements.summary: The public nomination policy confirms that decisions are maintained in a Stanford-login sheet. That sheet was not accessed. Open example-based areas may admit approved additions, but a nomination alone is not course approval.

requirements.title: Capstone approval and integrative timing
requirements.summary: The concentration advisor and SymSys office approve the capstone plan by the end of the first week of junior winter (eighth undergraduate quarter). Each component carries at least three units. The integrative requirement is no earlier than junior year and its units apply to the concentration; the practicum remains a separate host-core component.

requirements.title: Standard integrative option 1
requirements.summary: Eligible standard route: continuation of SYMSYS 190 from the honors practicum; this is not an unrelated first honors tutorial.

requirements.title: Standard integrative option 2
requirements.summary: Eligible standard route: a SYMSYS 195-series project course or CS 177 meeting the stated integrative project criteria. The series is an open course-number criterion, not an invented single course.

requirements.title: Standard integrative option 3
requirements.summary: Eligible standard route: faculty-supervised, approved symbolic-systems research registered through SYMSYS 196 or one of the displayed departmental research courses. The research/approval condition remains required.

requirements.title: Alternative to concentration-specific integrative course
requirements.summary: The three standard routes are alternatives to the concentration-specific integrative course pool, not extra courses on top of it. The separate public presentation/core practicum requirements belong to the host major; they are not recast as extra concentration electives.

notes: First-offered date is unknown; neither the catalog year nor an update date establishes a launch.

No concentration-specific assessed outcomes, descriptions, prerequisites, public course sites or example syllabi were verified in this bounded pass. Course titles and identities are observed; unknown exact course credits remain null.
The public document view explicitly permits anyone with the link without signing in. HTTP refresh sees only its JavaScript shell, so document extraction is a separate rerunnable public-export parser.
Cross-list aliases in parentheses are not silently counted as additional courses. HAI Human Impact and Augmenting Human Capabilities lists are examples under open criteria, not exhaustive pools.
Fall 2020 describes G4 core implementation, not first offering of this concentration.

Public policy closure on 2026-10-11 adds standard Core integrative routes, declaration/advising, grade/unit/overlap rules and transfer/replacement procedures. These do not remove the private approved-nomination boundary.

Capstone sources distinguish the integrative concentration component from the host-core practicum and public-presentation requirements. Standard integrative routes are alternatives to concentration-specific integrative courses, not extra required courses.

The public core page is updated April 2, 2026; the linked concentration documents remain dated September 27, 2024. The applicable-version policy is preserved without treating either date as a launch date.
